craft_claim: Repeated deflation habituates — each replay of the same irreverence loses arousal value — so the register must pause or move rather than escalate the same gesture.

supporting_evidence.note: Berlyne's arousal-potential framework holds that collative stimuli (novelty, complexity, surprise) lose their arousing power through repeated exposure — satiation — which is why the second identical deflation provokes less than the first.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 112(3):431-455
supporting_evidence.note: Audiences punish humor that violates their norms — repeated out-of-key deflation compounds the status cost rather than being forgiven as a running gag.

counterevidence.note: HONEST NULL: no experimental study of irreverent-prose saturation was found in this research pass. The mechanism rests entirely on adjacent arousal/satiation literature cited at whole-work level; the claim is therefore scoped as limited confidence.

scope: Long-form and serial work where the same move (same target type, same deflation cadence) recurs; also guides beat spacing within a single piece.
exceptions: Running gags that vary the setup (escalating variants, changing targets) can defeat simple habituation — but that is variation, not repetition.
Where a reader's appetite for the register is low from the start (individual differences in tolerating irreverence were not studied here), even first use can tire.
